parole.testo: Inherited from Maghrebi Arabic, from a Berber language. Compare Tunisian Arabic فكرون (fakrūn), Moroccan Arabic فكرون (fakrūn).
Inherited from dialectal Maghrebi Arabic (compare Tunisian Arabic فَلّوس (fallūs), Libyan Arabic فِلُّوس (fillūs), Moroccan Arabic فلوس (fallūs)), from a Berber language, from Latin pullus.
From Maghrebi Arabic, from a Berber language. Compare Libyan Arabic قرجومة (garjūma), Moroccan Arabic قرجوطة (qarjūṭa).

parole.testo: From Arabic كُسْكُس (kuskus), also كُسْكُسُو (kuskusū), from a Berber language.
From a dialectal Arabic lallūš or lālūš, said to be of Berber origin.
Inherited from dialectal Arabic, itself from Berber; compare Central Atlas Tamazight ⵜⴰⵏⴰⵖⵓⵜ (tanaɣut).

From dialectal Arabic; compare Tunisian Arabic حشلاف (ḥušlāf, “hay, dried-out grass or plant”). Further origin uncertain, though Berber origin has been suggested.
From Arabic زَنْبُوج (zanbūj), زَبُّوج (zabbūj), eventually probably from Berber. Compare Moroccan Arabic زبوج (zabbūj, “(wild) olive tree”), Tunisian Arabic زبوز (zabbūz, “(wild) olive tree”).

From a Maghrebi Arabic form akin to Moroccan Arabic جران (jrān), from a Berber language; compare Northern Saharan Berber ajru and Tashelhit agru. Possibly from an alteration of Latin rāna with initial g- imitating the croaking sound of a frog, as in Catalan granota and French grenouille.
